subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Should OpenClaw define explicit final-summary owner modes or a durable final-delivery obligation for detached/migrated subagent work, and should #80450 remain the canonical design thread for that contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent shape affects runtime ownership, delivery defaults, plugin/tool API, persisted state, and compatibility semantics.

options.title: Use existing delivery substrate
options.body: Define the contract on top of the current subagent delivery/steering state, keep existing defaults, and require docs plus live channel proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to obligation first
options.body: Track a durable delivery obligation and evidence state before exposing named owner modes to model or plugin callers.

options.title: Close as sufficient
options.body: Close this design thread only if maintainers decide current requester/session routing plus adjacent concrete bug issues already cover the product need.

recommendation.title: Use existing delivery substrate
recommendation.body: Define the contract on top of the current subagent delivery/steering state, keep existing defaults, and require docs plus live channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent delivery-state and docs history plus adjacent product/API review context make this the best available owner for the contract decision.
